modules.module_title: Design and develop finalized 3D models and product — Core Assessment Criteria

pcs.pc_description: Incorporate DfAM (Design for Additive Manufacturing) principles to optimize the design methodology based on 3D printing technology.
Evaluate part consolidation, geometric freedom, and biomimicry to enhance design capabilities.
Consider key process-specific, material- driven design guidelines, rules, and considerations.
Consider limitations of 3D printing parts, pre- defined design allowables in line with industry standards to comprehend design feasibility
Include suggested material types, colors, infill levels, orientations, and finishing methods in the 3D design.
Evaluate the constraints in physical properties of materials, including supports for overhangs, walls, and corners
Determine shapes of components with fewer stress points, smaller footprints, and superior mechanical properties
Decide on the minimum level of detail required based on the specific 3D printing technology.
Quantify and prioritize necessary mechanical properties, standards, and loads for the parts.
Refer to industry standards for applicable mechanical properties, including tensile, compression, flexural strength, and wear resistance
Analyze loading conditions to design parts such that largest forces traverse planes parallel to the print bed for optimal strength
Identify critical dimensions and features, including minimum wall thickness and support variables, adjusting for printer precision
Maximize print bed contact to minimize the need for supports and improve bed adhesion.
Orient the part optimally so the largest face lies on the print bed unless dictated otherwise by strength or geometry
Reduce supports and improve overhangs by optimizing angles to decrease printing and processing time
Avoid large flat surfaces and use rounded corners to prevent warping during printing.
Use fillets or chamfer edges to ensure smooth transitions and reduce stress concentrationS
Thicken vulnerable areas and appendages from the core to prevent breakage
Conduct operations between software systems to enhance workflows and design capabilities
Compare CAD modeling software solutions to identify the most suitable package for 3D printing technology
Incorporate AI-driven generative design methodologies and software tools for innovative solutions
Set part parameters like mount points and environmental stresses without strictly dictating the shape of the object
Extract and modify geometries generated by AI-based algorithms in CAD systems
Design and create special effects, including particle effects and dynamic simulations
Utilize software solutions to automate design workflows through scripting
Define target user needs and product requirements to ensure alignment with market expectations
Analyze product lifecycle and sustainability, considering recyclability and environmental impact.
Use feedback from prototype testing and user trials to iteratively improve product design.
Establish quality assurance protocols for testing prototypes to ensure functionality and compliance.
Ensure alignment with branding and aesthetic considerations to create products that resonate with target audiences
Establish quality assurance protocols for testing prototypes to ensure functionality and compliance with specifications
Ensure alignment with industry standards for applicable mechanical properties.
Plan for manufacturability (DfM) by considering cost-effectiveness during production

modules.module_title: Structure and conduct appropriate simulation tests, design — Core Assessment Criteria

pcs.pc_description: Perform multiple simulation runs to ensure the design is compatible with the chosen manufacturing processes
Aim to enhance the maximum pre-print accuracy of the CAD models by creating various test scenarios in iterations
Start with simple models and gradually modify them as the simulations present plausible results.
Create a detailed project plan to accommodate multiple iterations of FEA and TO (Topology Optimization) simulations coherently
Establish a clear set of success criteria for simulations based on project goals and performance targets to ensure results align with intended outcomes.
Conduct Finite Element Analysis (FEA) to understand and quantify the effects of real-world conditions on a part or assembly
Research and select from the most advanced FEA simulation software packages best suited for the analysis requirements.
Determine and prioritize various types of FEA simulations like structural, thermal, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), etc., based on the process, materials, and necessary performance indicators.
Generate a mesh model and refine the mesh using an iterative process of the FEA theory.
Define element type, choose material data set, and assign all the properties required
Enter sections and assign all the loads, constants, and boundary conditions according to the type of simulation
Request the data output according to the variables you want to study, i.e., forces, displacements, stresses, strengths, etC
Analyze the data by plotting contours of the requested variables, evaluating the deformed and undeformed shapes plots in the form of custom tabular reports.
Obtain a detailed visualization of where structures bend or twist, and the distribution of stresses and displacements as results.
Utilize sensitivity analysis to understand how variations in input parameters affect simulation outcomes.
Verify if the upper limits of failure meet the required mechanical properties, standards, and loads as anticipated
Consider redesigning the models based on the results for further analysis.
Incorporate advanced simulation techniques such as multi-physics simulations that combine thermal, structural, and fluid dynamics analyses when necessary
Validate simulation results with physical testing of prototypes to verify accuracy and refine models based on observed discrepancies
Perform Topology Optimization (TO) after the initial FEA simulation results check out for optimal material distribution layout.
Select from the available list of specific TO software solutions or the usual CAD packages.
Conduct topology optimization using the Finite Element Method (FEM).
Aim to optimize material layout within a predefined set of loads, conditions, and constraints.
Maximize the performance and efficiency of design by removing redundant material from areas that do not need to carry significant loads.
Solve design challenges like reducing unnecessary weight, resonance, and thermal stresses (e.g., lattice structures)
Determine the minimum allowable design space necessary for shape optimization of the product
Use TO software to test the structural integrity and identify unnecessary material under various simulated stress scenarios.
Implement the design modifications continuously as indicated by the simulation test outcomes
Analyze cost implications associated with different design optimizations to ensure that performance improvements do not significantly increase production costs.
Train and mentor team members on best practices in simulation methods and software usage to enhance overall team capabilities

modules.module_title: Export print-ready digital design files and generate tools — Core Assessment Criteria

pcs.pc_description: Transform the raw design files and renders into 3D printable digital file formats as Polygon Mesh models.
Select from different file formats to export like STL, STEP, IGES or IGS, OBJ, 3MF, or DXF, with STL being the most commonly preferred format
Employ appropriate methods to export based on the CAD program being used.
Consider the parameters used for outputting an STL file and their effect on the faceting of the mesh model.
Understand that smoother/less faceted surfaces (higher poly count or triangulation) result in larger STL file sizes
Determine factors like chordal tolerance or deviation, angle control, and minimum triangle side length.
Strike a balance between the model, desired surface fidelity, and the 3D printing process of choice, as 3D printing can only accept a certain size
Adjust the values of the chordal and angular tolerance to generate the optimal file size and mesh faceting without compromising on resolution.
After generating the mesh, ensure supports are created for the mesh model intelligently
Use mesh repair tools to check, repair, and optimize the mesh before slicing
Process the STL file using a slicer or slicing software to generate automated tool paths.
Convert the model into a series of thin layers through the slicer, producing a G-code file (.gcode) containing instructions tailored to a specific type of 3D printer
Determine optimal printing build parameters in the slicing software with regard to necessary mechanical properties, standards, and load requirements.
Input parameters like orientation, fill pattern, layer thickness, print speed, temperature, and other printer-specific settings.
If needed, modify model specifications partially through scaling features in the slicer before processing
Select the right slicing software based on organizational preferences, as the choice of slicer will impact the final print quality.
Utilize advanced slicing features such as adaptive layer height for optimized print quality and reduced print time
Implement support structures intelligently, considering their impact on ease of removal and print quality
Conduct print simulations within the slicer to visualize potential issues and optimally adjust settings
Export G-code from slicing software and import the G-code file into the 3D printing software
Familiarize yourself with printer-specific G- code commands and syntax for manual adjustments if necessary
Analyze material flow and deposition in the slicer to ensure effective printing of complex geometries
Maintain a library of optimized profiles for different materials and settings for consistency in print quality
Conduct test prints with different settings to identify the best configurations for particular geometries or materials
